reviewer: claude-opus-5-5 (self-reported; requested effort high; neither self-verifiable)
blockerStatement: No finding blocks the scoped structural UNIT adoption of the exact reviewed N1 schema patch. Every item below is a qualification or an open gap carried forward, not a defect in the observed results.

findings.title: AMB-5 dispute-grant predicate scoping is unobservable by the frozen pack
findings.evidence: M1 (dispute grant drops the predicate_refs test) survived all 15 valid batches with 282 PASS and 0 FAIL, exactly as frozen.
findings.impact: A checker regression that lets a dispute grant for one predicate refuse a record of the same key under another predicate would go unnoticed by the 282 pack. That direction is over-refusal (fail-closed), not over-admission, so it is an availability or correctness gap, not an admission bypass.
findings.carryForward: AMB-5 stays OPEN. Closing it needs a new independently authored case, not a refit.

findings.title: N1 guard x weakened HEX64 interaction (OPT-M9-N1) not tested
findings.evidence: MUTANTS-FROZEN M9 optionalN1Killer: OPT-M9-N1 not included and not resource-authorized. The N1 guard relies on fieldtypes.is_hex64 being a full match; M9 shows the 282 pack catches a '$'-anchored HEX64 elsewhere (3 required plus 15 informational FAILs), but not on the N1 revocation-alias path.
findings.impact: The N1 guard and the HEX64 validator are both needed for the N1 property; only the guard is mutation-evidenced on the N1 path (C6 M13-N1).

findings.title: M11 and M12 detections are all exception-rooted
findings.evidence: Every library killer fails with 'exception TypeError'. The CLI killers fail with CLI_INTERNAL_ERROR exit 2, which cli.py's outer except turns into a structured refusal (stdoutIsJson true, stderrHasTraceback false).
findings.impact: The pack detects these type-guard removals because the checker crashes, not because it refuses gracefully. Fail-closed is preserved. The frozen mode KILLED_MIXED is honest about this; it must not be cited as predicate-logic coverage.

findings.title: Exception message fragments are interpreter-version dependent
findings.evidence: M12 messages read "cannot use 'list' as a set element (unhashable type: 'list')" (Python 3.14 wording; python3 resolves to /usr/bin/python3.14). The frozen fragment "unhashable type: 'list'" is a verbatim substring, so all M12 killers are decisive.
findings.impact: Decisiveness for exception kills is tied to the interpreter. A different CPython could change the wording and turn a decisive kill into KILLED_NONDECISIVE without any change to the checker.

findings.title: M9 changes a passing result object (B2-SCRIPT)
findings.evidence: Under M9, B2-SCRIPT PASSes with result f7a883e0 (REFUSED [ADM_SCHEMA], note on verifier_profile). Under M12 the same case is 849e105a.
findings.impact: The weakened HEX64 changes internal behaviour even where the oracle outcome is unchanged; the 56-hex verifier_profile check still refuses. This is not a kill and not blast radius. I did not resolve the baseline 849e105a object, so the exact delta is a hypothesis.

findings.title: Whole-log fail-closed availability effect of the N1 guard
findings.evidence: src-patched/mcpcat/admission.py:154-162: any schema-invalid sibling in the consumer-pinned record log adds ADM_RECORDS_SCHEMA and refuses every record checked against that log.
findings.impact: Security-correct (fail-closed), and consistent with the consumer pinning record_log_digest. Operationally, one malformed log entry denies admission for all records under that log. This is accepted design, not a defect; it should be documented for consumers.

findings.title: Independence and oracle grade
findings.evidence: Every author and reviewer is the same model id (context independence only). The N2 cohort (23) is a consistency set, not an independent oracle. AUTH50 is same-author (C4 RESULT evidenceLabel 'AUTH (same-author expectations)'). The 282 pack is the only independently authored oracle in scope.
findings.impact: Test grades are kept separate in REPORT.md. AUTH and N2 PASS results support but do not establish the property.

findings.title: CLI input-mutation evidence is post-hash only
findings.evidence: C6 POSTCHECK-QUALIFICATION records (batch 02 and 04): CLI rows carry result.inputFileSha256 post-call hashes and no inputsMutatedByCall before/after flag; root bookkeeping KeyErrors occurred after the children exited 0 with RESULT saved; no rerun and no refit. C5 CLI results likewise carry post-call inputFileSha256 only.
findings.impact: No library-style before/after mutation claim may be made for CLI rows.

findings.title: Network isolation not demonstrated; timeout binary is uutils coreutils
findings.evidence: C4 U-NET-PROBE SKIPPED; isolation rests on the unshare --net wrapper (sha 41c65e55) only. /usr/bin/timeout resolves to /usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/timeout (f84e76ea), not GNU coreutils. No C5 child timed out, so timeout semantics did not affect any result.
findings.impact: Root checked only the boundaries of inspected files; there was no full-system write audit. The C0 and C4 wrapper elapsed times are unknown.

findings.title: INDEX.json prose says 168 raw CLI observations; the file holds 108
findings.evidence: C5-REVIEW-PARTS/INDEX.json 'format' text says '168rawCLI observations', the user brief repeats 168, but the same INDEX lists cli-observations.jsonl with 108 lines. I read 108 lines, which equals 12 mutants x 9 CLI rows (8 in batch 13 plus PC-F10 in batch 14). raw-cli-objects.jsonl holds 11 deduplicated objects.
findings.impact: Prose error only; no result is affected. 108 is correct by construction.

findings.title: No DECISION.json at the run root
findings.evidence: cardano-catalogue-v12-n1-run-20261015/DECISION.json does not exist. PRE-LAUNCH-COPIES.json names the decision at cardano-catalogue-v12-n1-scoped-execution-decision-20261015/DECISION.json (sha 0ec71d60, as in INVOCATIONS.json). I followed that explicit reference and read it.

findings.title: C6 reproduces C1 at stdout-hash level
findings.evidence: RESULT-MANIFEST-C0-C4-C6: the STDOUT sha of every batch pair matches: C6-N1N2-00/C1-00 26027d20, 01 846116ca, 02 540953ba, 03 aa07f1c5, 04 a19b3794. M13-N1 is the patched admission.py with the single line bad_siblings = [] (MUTANT.json). OBSERVATIONS mutationDelta lists the same 8 FAIL ids for C6 as for C1.
findings.impact: Strong structural evidence that the 7-line guard is the operative change. C6 is a behavioural restoration, not a byte revert: M13 admission.py (2e343ab1, 17132 B) differs from src-current (7b8c1730, 16608 B).
